item.title: Retrospectively Reverse-Engineering Apple's Neural Engine
item.description:
📝 The M5 decision confirms that ANE's compute core remained still useful for transformers, but inside a different dataflow. Each compute core has 128 FP16 (or 256 INT8) parallel multiply-accumulate (MAC) lanes. Regarding resolution, it does fixed-point reduction with FP16 at readout.
🔗 Read more: https://eiln.github.io/posts/ane.html

item.title: Navier-Stokes Announcement
item.description:
📝 Navier-Stokes Announcement Date: 11 September 2026 The Millennium Prize Problems were unveiled by the Clay Mathematics Institute (CMI) at a meeting in Paris in 2000 to celebrate “The Universality of Mathematical Thought”. These problems encapsulate some of the most difficult challenges that mathematicians were grappling with at the turn of the millennium. The Clay Mathematics Institute September 11, 2026 Image: Wikimedia Commons, C.
🔗 Read more: https://www.claymath.org/news/navier-stokes-announcement/

item.title: Another way to leak traffic on Android has been discovered
item.description:
📝 Another way to leak traffic on Android has been discovered September 10, 2026 Privacy A newly discovered leak in Android allows any app to send traffic outside the VPN tunnel. Yet another leak was recently discovered in the Android network stack that allows a malicious app to send traffic outside the VPN tunnel, even when "Block all connections without VPN" is active. Technical details The leak involves telling Android to create a keep-alive UDP connection that is offloaded to the hardware Wi-Fi or cellular chip.
🔗 Read more: https://mullvad.net/en/blog/another-way-to-leak-traffic-on-android-has-been-discovered
